title: Record-Breaking Elemental Superconductivity in Tetralayer Kagome Borophene
authors: Yingnan Liu, Yan Liu, Renyu Duan, Menghui Wang, Meiling Xu, Hanyu Liu, Shoutao Zhang
abstract: Superconductivity above the liquid-nitrogen temperature remains rare in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where strong covalent bonding often yields high phonon frequencies but insufficient electron-phonon coupling. Here, using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory, we predict tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) stabilized by ABAB covalent stacking, as a liquid-nitrogen-temperature elemental superconductor. With a predicted critical temperature of 102 K, TKB sets a record-high value among previously reported elemental superconductors. Unlike known high-Tc boron-based superconductors dominated by in-plane sigma-bonding states and high-frequency in-plane B-B stretching modes, TKB realizes an out-of-plane s-pz-bonding-mediated pairing mechanism, in which interlayer s-pz bonding states at the Fermi level are strongly coupled to low-frequency out-of-plane vibrations of boron atoms. These results reveal a distinct out-of-plane pairing channel in multilayer borophene and establish covalent stacking engineering as a potential route for high-Tc superconductivity in two-dimensional materials.
summary: This theoretical study predicts that tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) is a record-breaking elemental superconductor with a critical temperature of 102 K. The high $T_c$ is attributed to a novel, stacking-activated pairing mechanism involving out-of-plane $s$-$p_z$ bonding states coupled to low-frequency lattice vibrations. This work establishes covalent stacking engineering as a promising route for designing high-$T_c$ 2D materials.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving high-temperature superconductivity in two-dimensional elemental crystals, where insufficient electron-phonon coupling (EPC) often limits $T_c$ below liquid-nitrogen temperatures.
main_result: The authors predict that tetralayer kagome borophene (TKB) can be a record-high-$T_c$ elemental superconductor with a critical temperature of 102 K.
method: The study employs first-principles calculations combined with fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory to model the superconducting pairing mechanism.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is ABAB-stacked Tetralayer Kagome Borophene (TKB). The theory focuses on the electron-phonon coupling mediated by out-of-plane (OOP) $s$-$p_z$ bonding states coupled to low-frequency OOP boron vibrations.
key_observables: Predicted critical temperature ($T_c$) of 102 K; strong total EPC strength ($\lambda = 1.78$); pronounced anisotropy in the superconducting gap ($\Delta_{nk}$).
important_parameters: The optimal structure is the tetralayer configuration; the pairing mechanism relies on low-frequency OOP vibrations; the study notes the necessity of exfoliation for intrinsic measurements.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on theoretical predictions from first-principles calculations, and the mechanism hinges on the unique OOP pairing channel activated by the specific ABAB stacking.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the OOP pairing mechanism, the screening workflow for borophenes, the TKB structure with orbital-resolved band structures, and momentum-resolved plots showing the superconducting gap and EPC strength.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of high-$T_c$ in 2D elements, then details the theoretical framework using first-principles calculations and Migdal-Eliashberg theory. It presents the TKB structure and its unique OOP pairing mechanism, culminating in the prediction of the record-high $T_c$ and discussing the implications of stacking engineering.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the detailed analysis of orbital-selective coupling and lattice vibrations (phonons) provides a rich model for understanding electron-phonon interactions in low-dimensional systems, which has parallels in strongly correlated electron physics.
